summary: Repaired the SQLite v1→v2 migration on node1. The upgrade is atomic, repeat-safe, preserves existing data, defaults price_cents to zero, enforces nonnegative prices, and survives reboot. The OS release and kernel remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Rewrote bin/upgrade.py to use one transaction with rollback on any failure.
Added price_cents INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (price_cents >= 0).
Validated successful and repeated upgrades on a database copy.
Injected a post-ALTER failure and confirmed complete rollback to usable v1.
Upgraded the live catalog and verified IDs 1/2 and descriptions Paper/Tape were retained.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified persistence and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Atomic upgrade, repeat safety, and usable v1 database after failure
evidence.summary: Two successful runs produced v2; an injected failure after ALTER left version 1, the original columns and rows, and integrity status ok.

evidence.requirement: Retain IDs/descriptions and add nonnegative price_cents initialized to zero
evidence.summary: Live catalog contains (1, Paper, 0) and (2, Tape, 0); its CHECK constraint rejects negative prices.

evidence.requirement: Advance schema_version only after the complete upgrade succeeds
evidence.summary: The repaired code updates schema_version inside the same transaction after ALTER; forced failure leaves v1, while successful completion produces version 2.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel

evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID f1afbc7f-689a-477e-99b4-358a1d1d8226 was captured, safe reboot acknowledged, new boot ID 7a5685e4-ed83-4ce4-93f3-b6daf7dc99c6 observed, and the migration script plus integrity-ok v2 catalog recovered with identical rows and enforced constraints.
